claims.text: High-temperature annealing induces short-range order in refractory high-entropy alloys.
Short-range ordering enhances yield strength through increased lattice distortion that impedes dislocation motion.
Short-range ordering enhances thermoelastic response by modifying phonon scattering.
The as-cast refractory high-entropy alloy is a largely random solid solution with minimal short-range order.
Annealing at high temperature promotes atomic diffusion and formation of short-range order.
Short-range order takes the form of atomic clustering that increases local lattice distortion.
The ordered or clustered regions produce stronger dislocation-pinning sites.
Enhanced atomic mobility during annealing allows specific solute species to cluster.
Local lattice distortions associated with clusters hinder dislocation movement.
Hindering dislocation movement increases yield strength.
The annealing-induced lattice modification changes phonon scattering and thereby alters elastic moduli and thermal-expansion behavior.
The annealed alloy will have higher yield strength than the as-cast baseline.
The annealed alloy will have higher high-temperature elastic moduli than the as-cast baseline.
The annealed alloy will have a lower thermal-expansion coefficient than the as-cast baseline.
The annealed alloy will exhibit improved elastic recovery during cyclic thermal testing.
Oxidation or grain growth caused by unsuitable annealing conditions can overshadow the effects of short-range ordering.
Complex diffusion kinetics in multi-principal-element alloys make the amount of short-range order and resulting property changes uncertain.
